title: Base change along a directed colimit of rings: elements and zero elements come from a stage
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set, $(A_i,\alpha_{i'i}:A_i\to A_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ a directed system of commutative rings with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\alpha_i:A_i\to A$. Let $0\in I$ and $M_0$ an $A_0$-module. For $i\ge0$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-algebra via $\alpha_{i0}$ and $A$ via $\alpha_0$, and put $M_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}M_0$, $M=A\otimes_{A_0}M_0$, with the maps $\mu_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'i}\otimes\mathrm{id}:M_i\to M_{i'}$ ($0\le i\le i'$) and $\mu_i=\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id}:M_i\to M$. Then (1) every element of $M$ is $\mu_i(t)$ for some $i\ge0$ and some $t\in M_i$; (2) if $t\in M_i$ satisfies $\mu_i(t)=0$, then $\mu_{i'i}(t)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$. (Equivalently, $M$ with the maps $\mu_i$ is the colimit of the directed system $(M_i,\mu_{i'i})_{i\ge0}$ of $A_0$-modules.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits, line 1934: $\colim(M_i\otimes N)\cong(\colim M_i)\otimes N$) with the description of directed colimits, Lemmas Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778) and Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit, line 811); used implicitly in the proof of Lemma Tag 07RI (line 47654: 'Thus for sufficiently large $i$ we can find elements ...', 'on increasing $i$ if necessary ... since this is true in the limit')

proof.text: *Step 1 (the systems over $I_0$).* Let $I_0=\{i\in I:i\ge0\}$. It is a directed set: it contains $0$, and for $i,j\in I_0$ an upper bound $k\in I$ of $i,j$ (which exists as $I$ is directed) satisfies $k\ge i\ge0$, so $k\in I_0$. For $i\in I_0$ the $A_0$-module structure of $A_i$ is $c\cdot b=\alpha_{i0}(c)b$, and that of $A$ is $c\cdot a=\alpha_0(c)a$. Since $\alpha_{i'i}\circ\alpha_{i0}=\alpha_{i'0}$ and $\alpha_i\circ\alpha_{i0}=\alpha_0$ and the $\alpha$'s are ring maps, $\alpha_{i'i}(c\cdot b)=\alpha_{i'0}(c)\alpha_{i'i}(b)=c\cdot\alpha_{i'i}(b)$ and likewise $\alpha_i(c\cdot b)=c\cdot\alpha_i(b)$: the maps $\alpha_{i'i}$ ($0\le i\le i'$) and $\alpha_i$ ($i\ge0$) are $A_0$-linear. Hence $\mu_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'i}\otimes\mathrm{id}$ and $\mu_i=\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id}$ are well defined $A_0$-linear maps, and from $\alpha_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\alpha_{i''i'}\alpha_{i'i}=\alpha_{i''i}$, $\alpha_{i'}\alpha_{i'i}=\alpha_i$ and $(f\otimes\mathrm{id})(g\otimes\mathrm{id})=fg\otimes\mathrm{id}$ (checked on the generators $b\otimes m$) one gets $\mu_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\mu_{i''i'}\mu_{i'i}=\mu_{i''i}$, $\mu_{i'}\mu_{i'i}=\mu_i$: $(A_i,\alpha_{i'i})_{i\in I_0}$ and $(M_i,\mu_{i'i})_{i\in I_0}$ are directed systems of $A_0$-modules (Stacks, Algebra, Definition Tag 00D4, definition-directed-system) with cocones $(A,\alpha_i)$ and $(M,\mu_i)$.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00D4 (definition-directed-system, line 715); the A_0-module structures and the restriction to i >= 0 are the conventions of Lemma Tag 07RI (lemma-colimit-etale, line 47654), written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 2 ($A$ is the colimit of the $A_i$ as $A_0$-modules).* We show that $(A,(\alpha_i)_{i\in I_0})$ is a colimit of $(A_i,\alpha_{i'i})_{i\in I_0}$ in the category of $A_0$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Two facts on the ring colimit, $I$ being a nonempty directed set and hence a filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: (a) every $a\in A$ is $\alpha_j(b)$ for some $j\in I$, $b\in A_j$, by part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] with $R=\mathbf Z$ (commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebras are exactly commutative rings, every ring map being $\mathbf Z$-linear, so the colimit $A$ in commutative rings is the colimit in commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebras); choosing $i\in I$ with $i\ge j$, $i\ge0$ gives $a=\alpha_i(\alpha_{ij}(b))$ with $i\in I_0$; (b) for $i,i'\in I$, $b\in A_i$, $b'\in A_{i'}$ one has $\alpha_i(b)=\alpha_{i'}(b')$ iff $\alpha_{ki}(b)=\alpha_{ki'}(b')$ for some $k\ge i,i'$, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] (morphisms $i\to k$ of the category $I$ are the relations $i\le k$). Now let $(f_i:A_i\to P)_{i\in I_0}$ be $A_0$-linear maps with $f_{i'}\alpha_{i'i}=f_i$ for $0\le i\le i'$. Define $f:A\to P$ by $f(\alpha_i(b))=f_i(b)$ ($i\in I_0$, $b\in A_i$): every $a$ has this form by (a), and if $\alpha_i(b)=\alpha_{i'}(b')$ then by (b) there is $k\ge i,i'$ (so $k\in I_0$) with $\alpha_{ki}(b)=\alpha_{ki'}(b')$, whence $f_i(b)=f_k(\alpha_{ki}(b))=f_k(\alpha_{ki'}(b'))=f_{i'}(b')$; so $f$ is well defined. It is $A_0$-linear: given $a=\alpha_i(b)$, $a'=\alpha_{i'}(b')$ and $c\in A_0$, move both to a common $k\in I_0$, $k\ge i,i'$, so $a=\alpha_k(\beta)$, $a'=\alpha_k(\beta')$; then $a+a'=\alpha_k(\beta+\beta')$ and $c\cdot a=\alpha_k(c\cdot\beta)$ ($\alpha_k$ is additive and $A_0$-linear, step 1), so $f(a+a')=f_k(\beta)+f_k(\beta')$ and $f(c\cdot a)=c\,f_k(\beta)$. By construction $f\circ\alpha_i=f_i$, and $f$ is the only map with this property because the images of the $\alpha_i$, $i\in I_0$, cover $A$ by (a).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778: the directed colimit as the disjoint union modulo the relation, sums and scalar products computed at a common later index), applied to the underlying modules of a directed colimit of rings; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 3 (tensor products commute with the colimit).* By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits] with $R=A_0$, the directed set $I_0$, the diagram $(A_i,\alpha_{i'i})_{i\in I_0}$ with its colimit $(A,(\alpha_i))$ in $A_0$-modules from step 2, and $N=M_0$: $M=A\otimes_{A_0}M_0$ with the maps $\mu_i=\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id}$ is a colimit of the directed system $(M_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}M_0,\ \mu_{i'i}=\alpha_{i'i}\otimes\mathrm{id})_{i\in I_0}$ in the category of $A_0$-modules. This is the parenthetical 'equivalently' form of the statement.

*Step 4 (elements and zero elements come from a stage).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] with $R=A_0$, the nonempty directed set $I_0$ (a filtered category) and the colimit $(M,(\mu_i)_{i\in I_0})$ of step 3. Its part (1) says that every element of $M$ is $\mu_i(t)$ for some $i\in I_0$, i.e. $i\ge0$, and some $t\in M_i$: this is (1). Its 'in particular' says, for $i\ge0$ and $t\in M_i$ with $\mu_i(t)=0$, that $\mu_{i'i}(t)=0$ for some $i'\in I_0$ with $i'\ge i$: this is (2).

lean.statement: theorem directedColimitBaseChangeElementwise {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{v}) [HasColimit F] (i₀ : I) (M₀ : Type w) [AddCommGroup M₀] [Module (F.obj i₀) M₀] : let S := F.obj i₀ let R := colimit F letI : Algebra S R := (colimit.ι F i₀).hom.toAlgebra (∀ x : R ⊗[S] M₀, ∃ (i : I) (h : i₀ ≤ i), letI : Algebra S (F.obj i) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra let αᵢ : F.obj i →ₐ[S] R := { (colimit.ι F i).hom with commutes' := fun s ↦ congrArg (fun f : F.obj i₀ ⟶ colimit F ↦ f s) (colimit.w F (homOfLE h)) } ∃ t : F.obj i ⊗[S] M₀, αᵢ.toLinearMap.rTensor M₀ t = x) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (h : i₀ ≤ i), letI : Algebra S (F.obj i) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra let αᵢ : F.obj i →ₐ[S] R := { (colimit.ι F i).hom with commutes' := fun s ↦ congrArg (fun f : F.obj i₀ ⟶ colimit F ↦ f s) (colimit.w F (homOfLE h)) } ∀ t : F.obj i ⊗[S] M₀, αᵢ.toLinearMap.rTensor M₀ t = 0 → ∃ (i' : I) (h' : i ≤ i'), letI : Algebra S (F.obj i') := (F.map (homOfLE (h.trans h'))).hom.toAlgebra let αᵢ'ᵢ : F.obj i →ₐ[S] F.obj i' := { (F.map (homOfLE h')).hom with commutes' := fun s ↦ congrArg (fun f : F.obj i₀ ⟶ F.obj i' ↦ f s) (F.map_comp (homOfLE h) (homOfLE h')).symm } αᵢ'ᵢ.toLinearMap.rTensor M₀ t = 0)
